core_meaning.primary_meaning: Shifa represents Arabic شفاء (shifāʾ), meaning recovery from illness, healing, or a remedy. The lexical meaning is supported by Lane’s Arabic-English Lexicon.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Lane’s Arabic-English Lexicon defines شفاء as becoming free from illness or recovering, and by extension medical or curative treatment and a remedy. The word’s lexical meaning does not imply that a person named Shifa can heal others. Al-Shifa bint Abdullah is a historically documented female Companion whose given name is reported as Layla and who became known as al-Shifa; the historical by-name and the lexical word are related context, not proof that every use of Shifa refers to her.

faq.q: What does Shifa mean in Arabic?
faq.a: Shifāʾ (شفاء) means recovery from illness, healing, or a remedy in Lane’s Arabic-English Lexicon. This is the lexical meaning of the word, not a claim that every bearer has healing abilities.

faq.q: How is Shifa written in Arabic?
faq.a: The Arabic word is شفاء (with hamza at the end in the fully written form). Transliteration conventions vary; Shifa and Shifāʾ are common renderings.
The word شفاء (healing) occurs in the Qur’an, including 10:57, but that does not mean the Qur’an presents Shifa as a personal name. This entry makes that distinction.
The TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi entry identifies Al-Shifa bint Abdullah as a female Companion and notes that her given name was Layla; she became known as al-Shifa in connection with treating the sick.
Shifa is an Arabic word used as a personal name and is associated historically with Al-Shifa bint Abdullah. That historical association is not a ruling that the name is prescribed.

faq.q: What is the Arabic root of Shifa?
faq.a: Lane’s Lexicon files شفاء under the root family شفو and explains the word as recovery from illness, medical treatment, or a remedy. Root conventions can differ between dictionaries; this record follows the cited lexical entry.

faq.q: What does Shifa mean in Urdu?
faq.a: شفا کے معنی صحت یابی، شفا یا علاج ہیں۔ یہ لفظی معنی ہے، نام رکھنے والے شخص کی صحت یا صلاحیت کے بارے میں دعویٰ نہیں۔
A practical English approximation is shi-FAA; the Arabic form is shifāʾ, with a final hamza. Pronunciation may vary by language and family.

Shifa is used as a feminine personal name in many contemporary naming references, and the historical bearer associated with the name was female. This entry does not claim a measured gender distribution for every country.
